items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

This Pull Request has been created because #55353 breaks signed URLs for applications using the default ADC auth behaviour.

Detail

This Pull Request restores the previous behaviour where ADC is used when iam: true is set, but avoids excessive ADC calls by memoising the client. This means that calls are only made at instantiation time and when the credentials eventually expire (which the client takes care of). It also still allows overriding the auth used by either the mechanism suggested in #55353 (using Google::Apis::RequestOptions.default.authorization, which affects all clients) or by setting the authorization value on the IAM client directly.

This is necessary because the assumption in #55353 that the libraries will request auth themselves with the right scope isn't true in practice. So e.g this test when run locally and where GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS is set to the path to a service account key will fail with Google::Apis::AuthorizationError: Unauthorized. This is also what we have seen in production.

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

To fix the following scenario:

  • Call ActiveStorage::Blob#purge_later which calls ActiveStorage::Blob#purge.
  • System removes the blob record from the DB.
  • System tries to remove the file from the storage (ActiveStorage::Blob#delete).
    • It crashes, e.g., with a Google::Cloud::UnavailableError.
  • File stays in the storage, the DB record gallops to the sunset.
  • The file in the storage becomes orphaned and difficult to remove when we have hundreds of terabytes of data in the storage.

Details

This Pull Request allows removing ActiveStorage::Blob records only after their file in the service got removed successfully.

The provided solution

  • Checks if the blob can be destroyed.
  • Deletes its file from the service.
  • If the file deletion is successful, removes the blob record from the DB.

The with_no_destroy_preconditions_check method is added to avoid sending duplicate DB queries caused by attachments.exists?.

Alternative solution would be to wrap destroy and delete calls in a transaction, like below:

def purge
  ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
    destroy
    delete if previously_persisted?
  end
rescue ActiveRecord::InvalidForeignKey
end

I'd go with the transactional solution if there is no argument against it.

items.content_html:
Support for preloading instance-dependent associations was added here #42553.

Eager-loading instance dependent associations remains unsupported.

class Author < ActiveRecord::Base
  has_many :books, ->(owner) { }
end

Author.eager_load(:books)
# => The association scope 'books' is instance dependent (the scope block takes an argument). Eager loading
#   instance dependent scopes is not supported. (ArgumentError)

Author.joins(:books)
# => The association scope 'books' is instance dependent (the scope block takes an argument). Eager loading
#   instance dependent scopes is not supported. (ArgumentError)

And this also goes for associations with scopes with an optional parameter.

As far as I can tell, association scopes with an optional parameter don't currently have any use. I don't see how the argument could ever be nil outside of eager loading (which explicitly not permitted).

In my case, I've run into a scenario where I'd actually want a single association to behave differently depending on whether it's used for eager loading (or joining) or whether it's called on record. (I'm working on a temporal database gem for Active Record).

Something roughly like this:

class CategoryVersion < ActiveRecord::Base
  attr_accessor :as_of

  has_many :contemporary_products, ->(owner = nil) {
    owner ? where("valid_from > ?", owner.as_of) : where(valid_until: nil)
  }, class_name: "ProductVersion"
end

Anyways, if my assumption that optional instance dependent scopes currently can't be used, then I think this should be a safe addition that would allow the kind of conditional constraint behaviour that can be very useful in some cases.
items.title: Permit eager loading of optional instance dependent association scopes

items.content_html:
We should allow the DiskService to be configured

Motivation / Background

There are many times when I have a small or simple setup one a single server, and I want to be able to test my active storage download url for example. This change allows for syntax like the following:

  # config/environments/development.rb
  config.active_storage.service = :local
  config.active_storage.url_options = { host: "example.com", protocol: "https", port: 443 }
  
  # Extends the same convention as the existing actionmailer gem
  config.action_mailer.default_url_options = { host: "example.com", port: 8443 }

This Pull Request has been created because it is often the case that I do not have nor want to setup a full s3 integration, and I think it makes sense to give users the ability to opt-into more complete functionality if they choose to.

Detail

This Pull Request changes the disk service url options to have a fallback to an environment specific configuration if defined.

Additional information

This may not be the best implementation, it might make more sense to call ActiveStorage::Current.url_options=(value) during initialization.

This is what I have in my application as a workaround.

  config.active_storage.service = :local
  config.after_initialize do
    ActiveStorage::Current.attribute :url_options, default: { host: "example.com", protocol: "https", port: 443 }
  end

IMO I don't think I should put this snippet in an initializer because that spreads the configuration over multiple files without adding much. However this makes my environment inconsistent and more complicated that it should be.

We should consider that perhaps this DiskService should not depend on Rails directly, but we already have url_helpers method that depends on Rails, so I think this is not an issue. Users of activestorage without rails will have to always set url_options manually anyway.

Motivation / Background

This Pull Request has been created because the include_blank: true option in Rails form select helpers renders inconsistently across browsers, particularly in Firefox. The current implementation uses a single space character (" ") as the label for blank options, which causes visual rendering differences in Firefox compared to other browsers like Chrome and Safari.

This affects user experience as form elements appear differently depending on the browser, which is not the expected behavior for a consistent web framework like Rails.

Detail

This Pull Request changes the blank option label from a single space character to the proper HTML entity   in the following form helpers:

Files Modified:

  • actionview/lib/action_view/helpers/tags/select_renderer.rb - Updated add_options method to use raw(" ")
  • actionview/lib/action_view/helpers/form_tag_helper.rb - Updated select_tag method for consistency
  • actionview/test/template/form_options_helper_test.rb - Updated 12 test expectations
  • actionview/test/template/form_tag_helper_test.rb - Updated 3 test expectations
  • actionview/CHANGELOG.md - Added entry documenting the behavior change

HTML Output Changes:

<!-- Before -->
<option value="" label=" "></option>

<!-- After -->
<option value="" label=" "></option>

Affected Helpers:

  • select
  • collection_select
  • time_zone_select
  • select_tag

Additional information

This change improves cross-browser consistency without breaking backward compatibility. The functionality remains identical - only the HTML output is improved for better rendering consistency.

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

This Pull Request has been created because we have too many callback mechanisms to keep filter parameters, filter attributes, and encrypted attributes in sync. We can push the responsibility down to Active Support, and use it to filter event reporter payloads, request parameters, and record attributes.

Detail

This Pull Request removes callback classes because we don't really need them. We can instead use the recently introduced ActiveSupport.filter_parameters as a base source of truth for other frameworks to use as they need. While I was making this change, I also opted to pass a filter parameter to SQL logs originating from an Active Record model, so that subclasses with more specific filters can be used to filter.

Additional information

I failed to fix one bug here. Active Record filter attributes being stored on Active Record classes makes it so that filter parameters only apply immediately in eager-loaded environments. In local autoloaded environments where ActiveRecord::Base loading is deferred, parameter filtering for specific Active Record attributes won't work until the right model is loaded, which should be addressed at some point. This problem exists in the current implementation though, and will likely require deprecation of filter_attributes in Active Records, so we can do this later.

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

There are many rails gems out there that define active record classes to be consumed.

Sometimes, consumers of those gems want to override the properties, such as associations of the active record classes in the gem. When you override an association by redefining it using a concern, prepended module, etc, rails generally lets you do this and respect it. For example, passing association arguments such as disable_joins, foreign_key, inverse_of to has_many in an overriding class will change the original ActiveRecord Class' behavior (e.g. association.rb:45:219:360)

However, if you try to override the autosave option, it does not change the behavior of the underlying class.

class OriginalClass < ActiveRecord::Base
  has_many :items
end

class MyExtension
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  # Adding autosave: true here doesn't do anything
  has_many :items, autosave: true

  OriginalClass.prepend(self)
end

This is because even though you can override the reflection attached to the class, the original reflection is still referenced within blocks that define the methods related to autosaving associations. This means that the original reflection behavior (in this example, autosave: false) is still used.

Detail

This Pull Request changes the AutosaveAssociation behavior so that if a prepended module/subclass etc calls association methods (has_many, has_one, etc) that match an existing association on the class being modified, the old autosave association option value will be overwritten and the new value respected, like the behavior of other association options.

Additional information

The add_autosave_association_callbacks method are only defined when an association is first built; or in the example I gave above, when an association is rebuilt. I was not able to get this method to fire more than the number of times association helpers like has_many were called in the app with a specific association name. I don't think that checking if the method was already defined was buying any performance improvements, but it was preventing the existing behavior on a active record class from being overwritten.

I did consider an alternative that would keep the existing method defined checks but still allow for overriding the existing callbacks by passing a digest of the reflection. However, IMO this had more performance and complexity implications than what would be gained.

Alternative Approach

items.content_html:
Motivation / Background

Currently, ActiveModel::Validations allows passing a validation context to valid? and validate methods, enabling dynamic validation behavior based on context. However, persistence methods like create, update, find_or_create_by, etc., do not support passing validation contexts, which limits their usefulness in certain workflows.

This is particularly problematic when using methods like find_or_create_by, which rely on database constraint violations rather than validation failures. In such cases, we may want to skip specific validations (like uniqueness checks) while still maintaining them for normal create/update operations.

Detail

This Pull Request adds support for setting validation_context within blocks passed to ActiveRecord persistence methods such as create, update, find_or_create_by, create_or_find_by, and other similar methods.

Example usage:

class User < ApplicationRecord
  validates :email, uniqueness: true, unless: -> { validation_context == :skip_validations }
end

# Set validation context during creation
User.create(name: 'Test User', email: 'test@example.com') do |user|
  user.validation_context = :skip_validations
end

# Set validation context with find_or_create_by
User.find_or_create_by(email: 'test@example.com') do |user|
  user.name = 'Test User'
  user.validation_context = :skip_validations
end

This allows validations to run normally in most cases while selectively skipping them in specific workflows where database constraints are the primary safeguard.

Additional information

This change maintains backward compatibility as it only adds functionality when validation_context is explicitly set within the block. Existing code should continue to work without modification.
